item.title: US House blocks impeachment bid against Hegseth over Iran war
item.description: Republicans in the US House of Representatives on Tuesday blocked an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war, handing President Donald Trump a victory days after his party’s crushing midterm election defeat. The House voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee, effectively derailing a planned vote Wednesday on whether to bring formal charges against the embattled Pentagon chief. The resolution was introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, a Trump critic who was the only member of his party to oppose the procedural maneuver, according to US media. The impeachment drive had threatened to deepen Trump’s troubles after Democrats swept last week’s midterms, with anger at the sputtering Iran war and soaring fuel prices helping drive voters to a historic rejection of Republicans. Republicans still hold a narrow House majority until January, when Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress. And 11 Democrats missed the vote. Trump hailed the procedural defeat as an “EXONERATION of a Great American Patriot,” in a post on Truth Social, while Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell, in a post on X, called the vote as a “TOTAL VICTORY!” “We look forward to ending this sham impeachment in the committee room, where facts will continue to prevail and this distraction can be put to rest,” Parnell added. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. Rivers: Reconciliation Has Become an Electoral Asset Saturday’s Port Harcourt rally gave Tinubu something beyond a large political gathering: a public display of cooperation between Nyesom Wike and Governor Siminalayi Fubara. The President welcomed their reconciliation. Fubara pledged at least three million votes for Tinubu; an ambitious campaign undertaking that should be reported as a pledge, rather than an electoral projection. The strategic significance lies in organisation. Politicians who previously directed their energies against one another are presenting themselves as partners in the presidential campaign. If that cooperation extends through local structures, it could strengthen mobilisation. But agreement among leaders still has to survive competition over other offices, local grievances and differing expectations of political reward. Rivers also carries particular significance because Atiku Abubakar’s running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, is a former governor of the state. The presidential contest therefore intersects with an established struggle over political influence. The next evidence to examine is whether cooperation on the platform produces coordinated work across communities and polling units. Atiku’s Campaign Must Sustain Confidence For the ADC, the immediate challenge remains the legal uncertainty surrounding its leadership and nominations. The campaign says it has filed an appeal and an application for a stay of execution against the November 5 judgment, and notified INEC. Reporting on those filings stated that the stay application had not been determined; filing an appeal does not itself suspend the judgment. The reports reviewed for this edition do not establish a subsequent order granting that relief. The distinction matters because supporters need accurate information about the campaign they are being asked to sustain. Atiku’s camp continues to allege political interference. Those allegations require evidence and a response from the institutions concerned. They cannot substitute for an authoritative account of the court orders and subsequent proceedings. Politically, uncertainty creates practical pressures: organisers need direction, candidates need reassurance and resources must remain available. The ADC’s task is to pursue its legal challenge while keeping its economic and security proposals before voters. A campaign consumed by defending its participation risks losing opportunities to explain its purpose. Obi’s Benue Visit Will Test Campaign Access The NDC has announced that Peter Obi is scheduled to visit Yelwata and hold a town hall in Makurdi on Wednesday, November 11. Its Benue governorship candidate, Terhemba Shija, has alleged plans to disrupt the visit. A Benue government official has denied that allegation. The visit remains forthcoming. The immediate requirement is straightforward: lawful political activity should proceed safely. A visit to a community affected by violence also demands sensitivity. Bereaved and displaced families should have the space to explain their circumstances, with their dignity protected. For Obi, the policy test will be whether solidarity is accompanied by credible proposals for security, recovery and livelihoods. For the authorities, the test is equal protection. Political disagreement provides no justification for obstructing lawful access to citizens. item.title: Police arrest Abuja man over alleged rape, cyberbullying of women
item.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has arrested a man, identified as Usman Mohammed, over alleged rape, sexual assault, cyberbullying and intimidation of women under the pretext of recovering debts owed to him. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement, saying the suspect allegedly targeted women, including widows and other vulnerable persons, through predatory money-lending practices. Adeh said the suspect was arrested on Friday, November 6, 2026, following a report received at the Lugbe Police Station at about 7:05 p.m., alleging that he had been intimidating, sexually assaulting and physically assaulting several women over debts owed to him. She said operatives from the Lugbe Division, led by the Divisional Police Officer, immediately launched efforts to track down the suspect. According to her, the suspect was traced to the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Lugbe, where police operatives moved to arrest him. However, he allegedly attempted to escape upon sighting the officers by speeding off in his vehicle. The police said the operatives gave chase and eventually intercepted him before he could gain access to the expressway. Adeh said preliminary investigations identified Mohammed as a resident of FHA Lugbe, who allegedly used debt recovery as a pretext to intimidate and exploit his victims. She alleged that, in his latest incident, the suspect lured a woman into his vehicle and drove her to a secluded location in Lugbe, where he sexually assaulted and raped her. The suspect allegedly forced the victim to strip naked and recorded videos of her private parts, which he subsequently used to threaten to expose her publicly and kill her if she failed to meet his repayment demands. The police spokesperson said Mohammed was currently in custody and undergoing further interrogation. She added that he would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, condemned all forms of violence, sexual exploitation, intimidation and cyberbullying. He urged residents, particularly vulnerable persons, not to suffer in silence but to report cases of abuse, threats, blackmail and other criminal activities to the nearest police station. The Command also provided emergency contact numbers for members of the public: 08032003913 and 08061581938. item.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity — UNHCR
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has said. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the influx was worsening an already difficult humanitarian situation in Niger, which hosts more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to the agency, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of deteriorating security conditions in northern Nigeria. UNHCR’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. The agency disclosed that about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa in October, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua during the same period. It added that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. UNHCR expressed concern over the harsh living conditions confronting displaced families, many of whom are staying in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. Some women, it said, were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported rising cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, disclosing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. It warned that the lack of proper documentation was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The humanitarian crisis, according to UNHCR, is further compounded by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in Diffa, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing pressure, the agency acknowledged the support of Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the provision of land for temporary shelters. However, it appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for urgent interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without access to essential humanitarian assistance. item.title: NERC approves N30bn for free meters, targets May 2027
item.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion for the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF), targeting the provision of free electricity meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerated metering of Band B customers. The Commission announced the approval in Order No. NERC/2026/121 on the operationalisation of Tranche C of the MAF, which took effect on November 2, 2026. Under the arrangement, the N30 billion will be allocated among the 11 electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NERC said the third tranche was designed to accelerate efforts to close Nigeria’s metering gap, with equitable distribution of meters across states within the respective DisCo franchise areas. The Commission directed the DisCos to conduct transparent procurement processes involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stocks. It said maximum procurement prices had been set based on the median national MAP online bid prices recorded during the September 2026 bid cycle. The order provides for payment to selected meter providers in two stages: 70 per cent upon verification of meter stock delivery and the remaining 30 per cent after confirmation of complete installation. NERC emphasised that all meters supplied and installed under the MAF programme must be provided to customers free of charge. It also directed that each meter must prominently display the name of the relevant DisCo, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription, “NOT FOR SALE”. The Commission further stipulated that where a DisCo initiates the relocation of an existing customer’s connection point for revenue protection purposes, the cost must be borne by the distribution company. It warned that sanctions would apply where defaults by DisCos impede or delay meter installation. To ensure transparency and accountability, the order also establishes monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements for the Fund Manager, DisCos and participating meter providers. All supply and installation contracts under Tranche C are required to be filed with the Commission, while the installation of all meters under the tranche must be completed on or before May 31, 2027. NERC urged electricity distribution companies and other stakeholders to comply strictly with the order, describing the initiative as part of efforts to close the national metering gap, strengthen revenue assurance, improve service delivery and protect electricity consumers. item.title: Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has resolved to prioritise communities that demonstrate environmental responsibility in its interventions to control erosion across the state. The decision was taken at the weekly State Executive Council (EXCO) meeting in Awka, where the government said communities engaging in practices that worsen erosion would no longer receive priority attention. The prohibited practices include sand excavation, indiscriminate felling of trees, deforestation, dumping of refuse in drainage channels and directing stormwater onto roads. The State Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, who disclosed this after the meeting, said perpetrators of such practices would also be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others. Anambra has more than 1,000 active erosion sites affecting communities across the state, with experts arguing that addressing the scale of the problem would require federal and international intervention. Also at the meeting, the EXCO directed that Ogbodi in Amichi community, Nnewi South Local Government Area, which was recently cut off by gully erosion, should be reconnected within two weeks through palliative measures. Mefor said the process of identifying a permanent solution to the erosion problem would commence immediately. The erosion had cut off Ogbodi residents from other parts of Amichi, disrupting access and movement within the community. Meanwhile, the State EXCO approved what it described as the “Soludozie Anambra Framework”, an organised and inclusive platform designed to promote development through the Public-Private-Community Partnership (PPCP) model. According to Mefor, the initiative is intended to provide a structured channel through which Anambra indigenes at home and in the diaspora, as well as other well-meaning individuals, can partner with the state government to drive development. He explained that under the framework, the government’s role would generally be limited to documentation, recognition and support where requested, while donors and partners would directly manage their funds and projects. Mefor said the initiative was aimed at positioning Anambra as a model of collective governance and inclusive development, while accelerating the state’s development. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 11, 2026
item.description: The US dollar is trading at approximately ₦1,350 per dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), while the naira exchanges at between ₦1,411 and ₦1,419 per dollar in the parallel market on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Available exchange rate reports indicate that the official market rate was around ₦1,350.36 per dollar on Tuesday, November 10, while parallel-market dealers quoted buying and selling rates of approximately ₦1,411 and ₦1,419, respectively. At the parallel market, also known as the black market, the exchange rate varies depending on the location and the Bureau De Change (BDC) operator. The latest reported parallel-market figures indicate that Nigerians selling $1 to currency dealers could receive approximately ₦1,411, while those purchasing $1 may pay about ₦1,419. At the official market, the NFEM rate remains the benchmark for foreign exchange transactions in Nigeria. The difference between the reported official rate of ₦1,350.36 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,419 is approximately ₦68.64 per dollar. The exchange rate may change during the day depending on dollar supply, demand and trading activities across the foreign exchange market. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed currency dealers before carrying out foreign exchange transactions. item.title: Market conditions: Dangote Cement rescinds plan to list shares on London Stock Exchange
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Cement Plc, has rescinded plan to list its shares on the London Stock Exchange, LSE following market conditions. The company disclosed this after its Board Meeting held on Tuesday. In a statement sent to the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX and signed by Edward Imoedemhe Company Secretary, stated: “ This is to inform the Exchange, investing public and all stakeholders that at the meeting of the Board of Directors of Dangote Cement PLC held today, 10 November 2026, the Board resolved that, in light of current market conditions and the company’s strategic priorities, the company announces that it and its selling shareholder, Dangote Industries Limited (DIL) will not proceed with the proposed secondary listing and offering on the London Stock Exchange at this time. “ The company’s ordinary shares remain listed on the NGX, and this decision does not in any way affect the company’s operations or business plans. “Dangote Cement PLC remains focused on delivering sustainable value to its shareholders and building on its strong market position.” It will be recalled that Dangote had disclosed plans to list the cement business on the London Stock Exchange in May, eight years after an earlier attempt in 2018 failed. He had told the Financial Times that the proposed dual listing would involve selling about 10 percent of Dangote Cement’s shares on the UK exchange. What the metering schemes entail DISREP is a $500 million World Bank loan aimed at improving the financial and technical performance of DisCos. One of the major objectives of DISREP is to close the metering gap in the NESI by deploying 3.2 million smart meters. Installation of meters under the DISREP commenced in May 2025. A report in October 2026, citing the World Bank’s implementation report, said only 731,034 had been installed by September, representing 22.8 per cent of the target. PMI was approved in November 2023 to help address Nigeria’s persistent electricity metering challenges. It forms part of broader efforts to expand meter deployment, improve electricity-sector revenue collection and reduce reliance on estimated billing. The programme is a N700bn backed budget from the federation account and according to the Presidency, the project also includes training of over 5,000 Nigerians in meter installation and strengthening the capacity of local meter manufacturers in line with the Nigerian First Policy, among others. Also, the project is implemented by a federation-owned entity, PMI-Smart Grid Development Limited (PMI-SGDL), with the Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum and Governor of Kwara State, Mallam AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, serving as its board chairman. The Special Adviser on Energy to the President, Olu Verheijen, is the Executive Secretary, while Obafemi Solebo serves as the Project Director and Chief Executive Officer. Already, the training of 5,000 meters installers began in July, and it is being done in batches, with the third batch at the completion stage. According to documents from FAAC, PMI-SGDL received a first tranche of N120bn on May 13, 2024; a second tranche of N100bn was disbursed on June 10, followed by another N100bn on July 16. Another N100bn was disbursed on August 16, September 16 and October 11, respectively while the last N80bn was disbursed on November 10, 2024. The ledger termed the receiver as State House: Smart Grid Development Limited e-collection account. Though the PMI is supposed to distribute 3.8 million meters, former minister Adelabu had stated that distribution would begin with 1.1 million meters by December 2025, while two million meters would be distributed annually over five years. Two years after the complete disbursement of the fund by FAAC, distribution is yet to begin. item.title: Tinubu Won 2023 Election On His Own, Buhari Didn’t Fully Support Him – APC’s Hassan
item.description: A spokesperson for the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Alwan Hassan, has said President Bola Tinubu won the 2023 presidential election against all odds, insisting that former President Muhammadu Buhari did not fully support his candidacy. Hassan said Tinubu secured victory largely through his own political strength, arguing that Buhari did not actively stand behind the APC candidate during the build-up to the election. He made the remarks on Tuesday during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , while discussing the president’s chances of securing re-election in 2027. During the interview, Hassan was asked whether Tinubu would benefit from the organic political structure and support base associated with his predecessor, particularly as the APC prepares for another presidential contest in the next two months. In response, the APC stalwart questioned whether Buhari had given Tinubu the full backing of his political structure in 2023. “Did he enjoy that in 2023? Did we enjoy Buhari’s support in 2023? Let the truth be told, we did not,” he said. ﻿ When asked whether he was suggesting that Tinubu won the 2023 election on his own, Hassan answered in the affirmative, maintaining that the former president did not fully support his successor’s ambition. “On his own. Buhari didn’t fully come out to support Tinubu,” he said. He further argued that Buhari did not actively campaign for Tinubu during the 2023 election, despite both politicians belonging to the same political party. “Buhari didn’t do well in 2023. He didn’t actually come out to stand for us and stand for Asiwaju in 2023. Asiwaju won that election against all odds,” Hassan said. item.title: [VIDEO] Wike’s ₦10m Pledge: INEC, Police Can Trigger Investigation, Says Okoye
item.description: A former National Commissioner of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Festus Okoye, says the commission, the police and other law enforcement agencies can initiate an investigation into the ₦10 million pledge by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, to councillors ahead of the 2027 general elections. Okoye, a lawyer, said this on Tuesday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today. He said the absence of action by INEC would not prevent individuals or other relevant authorities from raising concerns or investigating the matter if an electoral offence was suspected. “If INEC is not taking this up, can anyone petition on this matter to say, I think Minister Wike is doing the wrong thing? Is it possible? Oh, definitely, yes,” he said. ﻿ The ex-commissioner added that the state could also initiate action if an offence had been committed, while law enforcement agencies could investigate where they believed there were grounds to suspect a violation. Mr Okoye said INEC could equally petition the relevant authorities to investigate the matter and prosecute anyone found culpable. Wike had pledged ₦10 million to each FCT councillor who successfully delivers their ward for President Bola Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the 2027 elections. item.content:encoded: The Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) has accused the Benue State Government of plotting to disrupt the planned visit of its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to the state, an allegation the government has dismissed as false. Obi is scheduled to visit Benue State on Wednesday for a town hall meeting in Makurdi and a humanitarian visit to Yelewata, where he is expected to pay tribute to victims of the June 2025 massacre and commiserate with their families. Addressing journalists in Makurdi on Tuesday, the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Terhemba Shija, called on the state government and security agencies to guarantee the safety of Obi and his supporters. Shija alleged that the government had issued threats aimed at preventing the former Anambra State governor from visiting Yelewata, recalling an earlier attempt to stop him from visiting the community. He said the party had notified the state government and security agencies of the planned visit, adding that its arrangements were already in place. “This letter addressed to His Excellency, the Executive Governor of Benue, was received on the 10th of November, which is today. “While we discuss with the security agency, all they require is that we should send them an itinerary of our visit. I’m going to soon embark on the visit of all the local governments. All I have told the DG to do is to write the itinerary, the times that we’ll be here, and then they will follow,” he said, displaying a copy of the correspondence. ﻿ Shija maintained that the party did not require permission from the state government to conduct its political activities but had notified the authorities in the interest of a peaceful visit. He described Obi’s planned trip as both humanitarian and political, saying the presidential candidate would lay a wreath at the cenotaph erected in memory of the victims of the Yelewata massacre along the Lafia Road. The NDC governorship candidate said Obi would also meet relatives of the victims but would not visit any government facility or internally displaced persons’ camp. According to him, the town hall meeting would be held at the multipurpose hall of the Mission House in Makurdi, behind the Benue Links head office in Wurukum. Shija alleged that the state government was unhappy with Obi’s visit because of its potential political implications ahead of the 2027 general elections. He also accused the government of being behind an earlier attempt to disrupt the presidential candidate’s visit to Yelewata, claiming that suspected supporters of the slogan, “No Alia, No Benue”, had mobilised to prevent him from accessing the community. He, however, urged Obi’s supporters to remain vigilant and peaceful, insisting that the party would not be deterred by the alleged threats. “The visit of Mr Peter Obi is going to be conducted in a peaceful atmosphere. We are not going to engage in any violence, but it must hold and it must be successful. The Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, will not yield to any blackmail or intimidation,” Shija said. Govt Denies Allegation Reacting to the allegation, the Benue State Government denied any plan to disrupt Obi’s visit, describing the NDC’s claims as false, baseless and mischievous. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the Commissioner for Information and Orientation, Solomon Iorpev, said the government had no reason to prevent any Nigerian from visiting the state, including political figures seeking votes. “Benue is a land of hospitality, and every Nigerian is free to move within it, including those who seek our votes. The government has no reason to fear any visitor,” the statement read. A combo image of Alia and Obi The government also cautioned the NDC against using the Yelewata tragedy for political publicity, describing the memory of the victims as sacred to the state. “We mourn with the families of the victims every day. No one should turn that grief into a political stage, and no one should use a visit meant to console the bereaved as material for a publicity campaign,” it added. It also urged the NDC to ensure that its supporters and associates conducted themselves peacefully. “Let no one be left in doubt, though: security agencies will deal firmly with any criminal-minded person who attempts to cause disorder and disrupt the peace, whoever they work for,” the commissioner said. The disagreement comes amid heightened political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Benue Blockades Obi has had his humanitarian and solidarity visits to the state disrupted on two notable occasions, first in April 2025 and again on September 8, 2026. In April 2025, the administration of Governor Hyacinth Alia reportedly halted Obi’s planned visit to an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp, citing security concerns and protocol issues. On September 8, 2026, Obi’s convoy was reportedly blocked by suspected thugs on Gboko Road, near the Nigerian Air Force Base in Makurdi, as he attempted to visit and console families in Yelwata following a massacre. The crowd allegedly mounted roadblocks, threw objects and chanted, “Peter Obi, go back,” forcing him to turn back to avoid escalating tensions. Police arrested 46 suspects following the incident. ﻿ The September incident triggered political accusations, with the Benue State Government claiming Obi failed to follow proper protocol and coordinate security arrangements, while opposition figures alleged that the blockade was politically motivated. Despite the controversies, Obi has visited Benue peacefully on previous occasions, including during his 2023 presidential campaign, when he held rallies and engaged with stakeholders without major disruptions.
